title: Rational Method Peak Runoff & Storm Sewer Pipe Sizing (Q = C·I·A)
description:
A 12.0-acre commercial shopping center site is being designed. The land use breakdown is:

• Rooftops: 4.5 acres (C = 0.90)
• Asphalt Parking & Drives: 5.0 acres (C = 0.85)
• Compacted Turf & Landscaping: 2.5 acres (C = 0.20)

The overland flow length is L = 600 ft with an average slope S = 1.5% (0.015 ft/ft). Using the Kirpich formula for overland time of concentration:
t_c = 0.0078 · L^(0.77) · S^(-0.385) = 0.0078 · 600^(0.77) · 0.015^(-0.385) ≈ 15.0 min.

The 25-year design rainfall intensity from the local IDF curve is:
I = 125 / (t_c + 15) = 125 / (15 + 15) = 4.17 in/hr.

The storm sewer pipe leaving the site has a slope S_pipe = 0.0080 ft/ft (0.80%) and Manning's n = 0.012 (reinforced concrete pipe).

Determine:
1. The composite runoff coefficient C_comp = Σ(C_i·A_i) / ΣA_i
2. The peak stormwater runoff discharge Q_peak = C·I·A (cfs)
3. The minimum standard circular pipe diameter D (inches) flowing full

The peak runoff Q and required storm sewer diameter D are most nearly:

options.label: B
options.feedback: Correct! C_comp = 8.80 / 12 = 0.733. Q = 0.733 · 4.17 · 12.0 = 36.68 cfs. For a 36-inch (3.0 ft) RCP at S=0.008: Q_full = (1.486/0.012) · (π·3²/4) · (3/4)^(2/3) · (0.008)^0.5 = 63.3 cfs > 36.7 cfs. A 30-inch pipe yields only 37.5 cfs (too close to capacity), so standard design selects 36 inches.

options.label: C
options.feedback: Incorrect. Did you assume C = 0.85 for the entire site? You must use the area-weighted composite C = 0.733.

options.label: D
options.feedback: Incorrect. Double check Q = C · I · A calculation: 0.733 · 4.17 · 12 = 36.7 cfs.

hint: Step 1: C_comp = (4.5·0.90 + 5.0·0.85 + 2.5·0.20) / 12.0 = 8.80 / 12 = 0.733. Step 2: Q = C·I·A = 0.733 · 4.17 in/hr · 12 acres = 36.68 cfs. Step 3: Solve Manning's equation for pipe flowing full: D = [ (2.16 · Q · n) / S^(1/2) ]^(3/8) in feet.
shortcut: Remember in US customary units: 1 cfs ≈ 1 acre-inch/hour (actually 1.008 cfs). So Q = C · I · A directly in cfs! 0.733 · 4.17 · 12 = 36.7 cfs. D = [(2.16 · 36.7 · 0.012) / 0.008^0.5]^0.375 = [0.951 / 0.0894]^0.375 = (10.63)^0.375 = 2.44 ft = 29.3 in → Round up to next standard size 30 or 36 in.
fifthGrader: When rain falls on a parking lot and roof, it can't soak into the dirt, so it rushes away like a slide! We measure how much roof, pavement, and grass there is, multiply by how hard it's pouring, and size a huge concrete pipe underground so the parking lot never turns into a lake.

title: Detention Basin Storage Volume & Modified Rational Hydrograph Sizing
description:
A 15.0-acre site undergoing commercial redevelopment produces a 100-year peak post-development runoff Q_post = 48.0 cfs with a time of concentration t_c = 20 min. The municipal stormwater ordinance mandates that the peak discharge from the site must not exceed the pre-development 10-year allowable release rate Q_allow = 12.0 cfs.

Using the Modified Rational Method (triangular hydrograph approximation):
• Inflow hydrograph rises to Q_peak at time t = t_c and recedes at t = 2·t_d.
• For a critical storm duration t_d = 45 min (where rainfall intensity produces maximum storage deficit):
  Inflow volume V_in = Q_post(t_d) · t_d · 60 sec/min
  Outflow volume V_out = 0.5 · Q_allow · (t_d + t_c) · 60 sec/min

For a design rainfall intensity at t_d = 45 min yielding Q_in = 38.5 cfs:
Storage Volume Required:
V_req = [Q_in - Q_allow · (0.5 + 0.5 · t_c / t_d)] · t_d · 60
Or using triangular approximation: V_req ≈ (Q_in - Q_allow) · t_d · 60 sec/min.
With Q_in = 38.5 cfs and Q_allow = 12.0 cfs over t_d = 45 min:
V_req = (38.5 - 12.0) cfs · (45 · 60 s) = 26.5 cfs · 2700 s = 71,550 cu ft.

Convert this storage volume to Acre-Feet (1 acre = 43,560 sq ft):
V_acre-ft = 71,550 / 43,560 = 1.64 ac-ft.

The required detention pond storage volume in acre-feet is most nearly:

options.label: A
options.feedback: Incorrect. That assumes a short 20-minute storm duration, which does not govern the maximum detention volume.

options.label: C
options.feedback: Incorrect. That neglects the allowable outflow during the storm event (zero-discharge assumption).

options.label: D
options.feedback: Incorrect. Check your unit conversion: 1 acre-foot = 43,560 cu ft.

hint: Step 1: Compute net storage discharge rate ΔQ = Q_in - Q_allow = 38.5 - 12.0 = 26.5 cfs. Step 2: Multiply by storm duration in seconds: 45 min · 60 s/min = 2,700 s. Step 3: V = 26.5 · 2700 = 71,550 cu ft. Step 4: Convert to acre-feet: 71,550 / 43,560 = 1.64 ac-ft.
shortcut: Storage volume = Net rate × time. ΔQ = 26.5 cfs. Time = 45 min = 0.75 hr. 1 cfs for 1 hour = 3600 cu ft = 0.0826 ac-ft. So V = 26.5 × 0.75 × 0.0826 = 1.64 ac-ft!
fifthGrader: A detention basin is like a giant bathtub for rain. When a thunderstorm hits, water pours in way faster than the city pipes can handle. The basin catches the giant flood wave and lets it trickle out slowly through a small drain pipe so downstream neighborhoods don't get flooded!
